content_sections.heading: About the District Police Wellness Centre
content_sections.text: The District Police Office, Ernakulam Rural issued this notice under circular No. 13/2026/PHQ of the State Police Chief dated 23.09.2026 and letter No. A2-3197/2026/SPD of the Social Policing Directorate dated 16.10.2026. The post is meant to ensure the mental health and welfare of police personnel and their families. The Clinical Psychologist will work at the District Police Wellness Centre established in Ernakulam Rural district.

content_sections.heading: Where and How to Send
content_sections.text: Send the application to: The District Police Chief, District Police Office, Ernakulam Rural, Aluva, PIN - 683101. The notice does not name the postal mode, a form to use, or what to write on the envelope. It does not ask for an email application. Along with the application, enclose attested copies of the certificates proving age and qualification, a bio-data and passport size photographs. For further details the notice gives the phone number 0484-2633550 and the email [email protected] . The letterhead also prints [email protected] and 04842624455.

content_sections.heading: Posts, Eligibility and Pay
content_sections.text: A Clinical Psychology qualification recognised by the Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI); OR a postgraduate degree in Psychology / Clinical Psychology / Applied Psychology, followed by a two-year full-time M.Phil in Clinical Psychology. A valid registration with RCI. Preference is given to candidates with prior experience of counselling police personnel in psychotherapy and crisis intervention, for not less than two years. Proficiency in Malayalam and English. Computer literacy. Medical fitness and a character certificate are also listed. Maximum 35 years. The notice prints no age cut-off date and no age relaxation. Candidates should check the official notification for the discipline-specific eligibility of the post.

content_sections.heading: Ernakulam Rural Police Clinical Psychologist Job Description
content_sections.text: Collect personal information, examine and evaluate it, and take the necessary action. Give personal, family and group counselling (stress management, anger control, conflict resolution, relaxation techniques). Intervene in cases involving the possibility of self-harm, suicidal thoughts, addiction or severe mental distress, and refer to higher treatment facilities where necessary. Maintain the records and registers of all cases. Ensure follow-up of all cases through appointment schedules. Keep case files (history, treatment plan, session notes, reviews) safely, separate from service and official records.

content_sections.heading: Enclosures
content_sections.text: Application Attested copies of certificates proving age and qualification Bio-data Passport size photographs

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection is based on qualification, prior experience, a written test and an interview. The written test carries 100 marks and is an objective type question paper. It covers Psychology, counselling techniques, psychological assessment, crisis intervention, suicide prevention, professional ethics and confidentiality. The minimum qualifying mark in the written test is 40. The interview carries 25 marks. The notice does not give the date or venue of the test or the interview.
